dedupe_keys.name: how undesired non idealities of the input signal affect the accuracy evaluation of instrument transformers at power frequency

description: Letizia, Palma Sara and colleagues publish this resource through the source community. Numerical simulations generate test voltage/current signals with varied total harmonic distortion and frequency deviation. Common processing algorithms estimate resulting power-frequency ratio and phase errors. Coverage is the influence of non-ideal calibration signals on grid instrument-transformer accuracy. The source reports that some industrial-laboratory uncertainty targets tolerate distortion above 2% with suitable algorithms; this is conditional on the stated uncertainty requirements. It does not replace the limits of a calibration standard or establish performance for every transformer. Zenodo supplies the descriptive publication with open access under cc-by-4.0. The publication does not establish public access to an implementation or its separate licence. A limitation is that complete implementation or measurement settings cannot be reconstructed from descriptive metadata alone. Related experimental components and publications retain their distinct roles; separate deposits are not assumed to provide independent observations.
